title: Natural geometric cohomology comparison on residue cycles modulo boundaries
statement: Let f:X to S and fi:Xi to S (i in Fin n) be flat proper locally finitely presented, and ui:Xi to X be over S. Let L be invertible. Let k:W to S be an immersion, w lie in the affine open U, and s=k(w). Supply a trivialization tau:L_s isomorphic to O_Xs. Supply the target coefficient trivializations over Xi times S U, and connective strictly perfect models K and C_i representing the restricted direct images, with C_i.d(0,1)=0. Set A=Gamma(W,U) and p=ker(A to kappa(w)). Write ZK=ker(dK(1,2) tensor kappa(p)) and Zi=ker(dCi(1,2) tensor kappa(p)). There are additive maps gamma:ZK to H1(X_s,O) and beta_i:Zi to H1(Xi_s,O), and derived arrows a_i:Q(K) to Q(C_i). Gamma is surjective; gamma(x)=0 if and only if x is the residue of an incoming degree-zero differential. For every chain representative phi of a_i and every x in ZK whose residue image y under phi^1 belongs to Zi, beta_i(y)=ui_s pullback(gamma(x)). No coordinate basis or source residue-differential vanishing is assumed; boundaries are retained. The geometric, perfect and cohomological notions are those of the parent statement [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-perfect-complex, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-sc-invertible-module, def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Construct coefficient pullback via the module adjunction, apply the derived direct-image functors, restrict to U and conjugate by the representing isomorphisms, defining a_i. Use the base-change maps with their canonical characterising property so their naturality squares are preserved.

Strictly perfect models have bounded flat terms, so termwise residue tensor computes derived tensor. Identify the affine residue field kappa(p) with kappa(w), then use the immersion to identify kappa(w) with kappa(s). Arbitrary derived base change identifies the resulting homology with the fibre direct-image homology. The affine-base comparison identifies its global sections with fibre cohomology.

Use tau on the source and its pullbacks along ui_s on all targets. Compose the quotient from source cycles to degree-one homology with the geometric identification to obtain gamma. It is surjective, and has exactly the incoming residue boundaries as its kernel. Compose the target cycle quotient with the target geometric identification to obtain beta_i.

For each chain representative of a_i, its localized homology map is the homology map of a_i. Naturality of the canonical base-change and affine cohomology identifications gives the equality on cycles. The common source trivialization tau ensures that coefficient pullback becomes structure-sheaf pullback.
